## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/how-to-analyze-single-cell-rna-seq-data-complete-beginners-guide-part-10-cell-cell-communication-analysis-using-nichenet/>

Part 2 of 2. Using the top ligands from part 1, this notebook visualizes the
ligand activities, predicts the target genes and the receptors of the top
ligands, shows which sender cell types express them, optionally runs the
extended multi-criteria prioritization (Step 12), traces a signaling path from
the top ligand to its top target gene, assigns each top ligand to its most
likely sender cell type and draws a circos plot of sender cell types and target
genes.

Part 1 must be run first (it requires tutorial 7 part 1 for its input object).
Part 2 reads `results/nichenet_part1_state.RData` and
`results/seurat_nichenet_input.rds` written by part 1 and reloads the prior
models from the cache folder.

Step 12 (extended prioritization) uses nichenetr functions
(`process_table_to_ic()`, `generate_prioritization_tables()`) exactly as in the
article; their signatures differ between nichenetr versions, so the step is
wrapped in `tryCatch()` and, if it fails, the error is printed and the rest of
the notebook still runs.

Code is taken from the source article's code blocks (steps 8-15). Changes made
for this notebook series: hard-coded values moved into the YAML front matter,
paths built from `params` rather than `setwd()`, and changes marked `ADDED:` or
`FIX:` in comments.

## Libraries and directories

```{r step1_libs_data}
#-----------------------------------------------
# Load libraries (as in STEP 1 of part 1)
#-----------------------------------------------
library(nichenetr)
library(Seurat)
library(tidyverse)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)
library(patchwork)

source(here::here("helper_functions", "params_read.R"))
params <- params_ingest()

# Working directories
base.dir <- params$base.dir
nichenet.dir <- file.path(base.dir, params$nichenet.subdir)
plot.dir <- file.path(nichenet.dir, "plots/nichenet")
result.dir <- file.path(nichenet.dir, "results")
for (d in c(plot.dir, result.dir)) {
  dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}

model.cache.dir <- if (nzchar(params$model.cache.dir)) path.expand(params$model.cache.dir) else file.path(base.dir, "nichenet_models")

# Set random seed for reproducibility
set.seed(params$seed)

# Column names from params
celltype.col <- params$celltype.col
condition.col <- params$condition.col

cat("Environment setup complete!\n")
cat("Seurat version:", as.character(packageVersion("Seurat")), "\n")
cat("nichenetr version:", as.character(packageVersion("nichenetr")), "\n")
```

## Visualize ligand activity scores

```{r step8_activity_barplots, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 6}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 8: Visualize Ligand Activity Scores
#-----------------------------------------------
# Helper to build a bar plot for one set of ligand activities
plot_ligand_activity <- function(ligand_activities_df, top_ligands, subtitle) {
  ligand_activities_df %>%
    filter(test_ligand %in% top_ligands) %>%
    mutate(test_ligand = factor(test_ligand, levels = rev(top_ligands))) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = test_ligand, y = aupr_corrected)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = params$bar.fill) +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(
      title    = "NicheNet Ligand Activity Scores",
      subtitle = subtitle,
      x        = "Ligand",
      y        = "Corrected AUPR"
    ) +
    theme_classic()
}

p_agnostic <- plot_ligand_activity(
  ligand_activities_agnostic,
  best_upstream_ligands_agnostic,
  paste0("Top ", top_n, " ligands — sender-agnostic")
)

p_focused <- plot_ligand_activity(
  ligand_activities_focused,
  best_upstream_ligands_focused,
  paste0("Top ", top_n, " ligands — sender-focused")
)

ggsave(file.path(plot.dir, "ligand_activity_barplot.pdf"),
       plot = p_agnostic + p_focused, width = 12, height = 6)
# ADDED: show the plot in the notebook
print(p_agnostic + p_focused)
```

## Predict target genes of top ligands

```{r step9_ligand_targets, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 9: Predict Target Genes of Top Ligands
#-----------------------------------------------
# Define a regulatory potential cutoff
# get_weighted_ligand_target_links extracts the top target genes
# for each ligand above a given threshold
active_ligand_target_links_df <- best_upstream_ligands %>%
  lapply(get_weighted_ligand_target_links,
         geneset              = geneset_oi,
         ligand_target_matrix = ligand_target_matrix,
         n                    = params$target.top_n) %>%  # consider top 250 targets per ligand
  bind_rows() %>%
  drop_na()

# Convert to a wide matrix for heatmap visualization.
# cutoff = 1/3 retains only weights above the 33rd percentile;
# prepare_ligand_target_visualization handles this filtering internally.
active_ligand_target_links <- prepare_ligand_target_visualization(
  ligand_target_df     = active_ligand_target_links_df,
  ligand_target_matrix = ligand_target_matrix,
  cutoff               = params$target.cutoff
)

# Order ligands by activity rank for consistent heatmap layout
order_ligands <- intersect(best_upstream_ligands, colnames(active_ligand_target_links)) %>%
  rev()
order_targets <- active_ligand_target_links_df$target %>%
  unique() %>%
  intersect(rownames(active_ligand_target_links))

# Generate the ligand-target heatmap
vis_ligand_target <- active_ligand_target_links[order_targets, order_ligands]

p_ligand_target_network <- vis_ligand_target %>%
  make_heatmap_ggplot(
    y_name    = paste0("Target genes in receiver (", receiver, ")"),  # receiver name from params
    x_name    = "Prioritized ligands",
    color     = params$target.heatmap.color,
    legend_title = "Regulatory\npotential"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(face = "italic"))

ggsave(file.path(plot.dir, "ligand_target_heatmap.pdf"),
       plot = p_ligand_target_network, width = 10, height = 8)
# ADDED: show the plot in the notebook
print(p_ligand_target_network)
```

## Identify which sender cell types express each top ligand

```{r step11_ligand_sender, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 11: Identify Which Sender Cell Types Express Each Top Ligand
#-----------------------------------------------
# For each sender cell type, check which top ligands it expresses
# get_lfc_condition computes log fold-change between conditions for each cell type
# Here we compute average expression of each ligand per sender cell type

# Get average expression across all sender cells (combined conditions, for simplicity)
# ADDED: the condition column name comes from params (the article's subset =
# condition %in% ... hard-codes it), so the cells are selected explicitly.
cells_oi_ref <- colnames(seurat_obj)[seurat_obj[[condition.col, drop = TRUE]] %in% c(condition_oi, condition_reference)]
seurat_sender <- subset(seurat_obj,
                        idents = sender_celltypes,
                        cells  = cells_oi_ref)

# Assign sender cell type as identity
Idents(seurat_sender) <- seurat_sender[[celltype.col, drop = TRUE]]

best_upstream_ligands <- intersect(best_upstream_ligands, rownames(seurat_sender))

# Compute mean expression of top ligands per sender cell type
# FIX: slot= is defunct in Seurat v5 AverageExpression(); layer= is used instead
ligand_expression_matrix <- AverageExpression(
  seurat_sender,
  features  = best_upstream_ligands,
  assay     = params$assay,
  layer     = "data"  # log-normalized values
)[[params$assay]]
# ADDED: AverageExpression may return a sparse matrix; scale() needs a dense one
ligand_expression_matrix <- as.matrix(ligand_expression_matrix)

# Scale for visualization
ligand_expression_scaled <- t(scale(t(ligand_expression_matrix)))
# FIX: ligands with identical expression in all senders give NaN rows after
# scaling, which make pheatmap's clustering fail; drop them
nan_rows <- apply(ligand_expression_scaled, 1, function(x) any(is.nan(x)))
if (any(nan_rows)) {
  cat("Dropping", sum(nan_rows), "ligand(s) with no variation across senders:",
      paste(rownames(ligand_expression_scaled)[nan_rows], collapse = ", "), "\n")
  ligand_expression_scaled <- ligand_expression_scaled[!nan_rows, , drop = FALSE]
}

# Heatmap: which sender cell type expresses each top ligand?
p_ligand_sender <- pheatmap::pheatmap(
  mat              = ligand_expression_scaled[intersect(best_upstream_ligands, rownames(ligand_expression_scaled)), ],
  color            = colorRampPalette(unlist(params$sender.heatmap.colors))(50),
  cluster_cols     = TRUE,
  cluster_rows     = TRUE,
  fontsize_row     = 9,
  fontsize_col     = 9,
  main             = "Ligand Expression Across Sender Cell Types",
  filename         = file.path(plot.dir, "ligand_sender_heatmap.pdf"),
  width            = 10,
  height           = 8
)
# ADDED: pheatmap(filename=) does not draw to the notebook; draw the returned gtable
grid::grid.newpage()
grid::grid.draw(p_ligand_sender$gtable)
```

## Extended prioritization (optional)

```{r step12_prioritization}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 12 (Optional): Extended Prioritization — Incorporating Expression and DE Information
#-----------------------------------------------
# ADDED: the whole step is wrapped in tryCatch(): the nichenetr functions used
# here (process_table_to_ic(), generate_prioritization_tables(), get_exprs_avg())
# have different signatures in different nichenetr versions. If it fails, the
# message is printed and the notebook continues with Step 13. Objects are still
# created in the global environment (tryCatch evaluates in the calling frame).
tryCatch({
  # Step 12a: Identify ligand and receptor genes present in lr_network
  lr_network_filtered <- lr_network %>%
    filter(from %in% potential_ligands_focused | to %in% expressed_receptors)

  ligands_in_lr   <- unique(lr_network_filtered$from)
  receptors_in_lr <- unique(lr_network_filtered$to)

  # Restrict to genes that actually exist in the Seurat object.
  all_genes_seurat  <- rownames(seurat_obj)
  lr_features <- intersect(unique(c(ligands_in_lr, receptors_in_lr)), all_genes_seurat)

  # Step 12b: Compute DE of all cell types vs all others, restricted to
  # ligand/receptor genes only (reduces compute time considerably)
  # Run on the condition of interest subset
  cells_oi <- colnames(seurat_obj)[seurat_obj[[condition.col, drop = TRUE]] == condition_oi]
  seurat_oi <- subset(seurat_obj, cells = cells_oi)  # condition column name from params
  Idents(seurat_oi) <- seurat_oi[[celltype.col, drop = TRUE]]

  DE_table <- FindAllMarkers(
    seurat_oi,
    features        = lr_features,
    min.pct         = 0,
    logfc.threshold = 0,
    return.thresh   = 1   # keep all genes regardless of p-value
  )

  # Step 12c: Compute average expression per cell type in condition of interest
  expression_info <- get_exprs_avg(
    seurat_obj,
    celltype_colname  = celltype.col,
    condition_colname = condition.col,
    condition_oi      = condition_oi,
    features          = lr_features
  )

  # Step 12d: Compute condition-level DE (ligand/receptor upregulation by condition)
  Idents(seurat_obj) <- seurat_obj[[condition.col, drop = TRUE]]
  condition_markers <- FindMarkers(
    seurat_obj,
    ident.1         = condition_oi,
    ident.2         = condition_reference,
    features        = lr_features,
    min.pct         = 0,
    logfc.threshold = 0
  ) %>%
    rownames_to_column("gene")

  # Step 12e: Format each table separately using process_table_to_ic().
  # The function is called three times — once per table type:
  #   "celltype_DE" : cell-type-level DE (FindAllMarkers output)
  #   "expression"  : average expression per cell type
  #   "group_DE"    : condition-level DE (FindMarkers output)
  processed_DE_table <- process_table_to_ic(
    DE_table,
    table_type   = "celltype_DE",
    lr_network_filtered,
    senders_oi   = sender_celltypes,
    receivers_oi = receiver
  )

  processed_expr_table <- process_table_to_ic(
    expression_info,
    table_type = "expression",
    lr_network_filtered
  )

  processed_condition_markers <- process_table_to_ic(
    condition_markers,
    table_type = "group_DE",
    lr_network_filtered
  )

  # Step 12f: Generate the multi-criteria prioritization table.
  prioritized_tbl <- generate_prioritization_tables(
    processed_expr_table,        # sender_receiver_info (average expression)
    processed_DE_table,          # sender_receiver_de   (cell-type DE)
    ligand_activities_focused,
    processed_condition_markers, # lr_condition_de      (condition-level DE)
    scenario = params$prioritization.scenario
  )

  # Save results
  write.csv(prioritized_tbl, file.path(result.dir, "prioritized_lr_pairs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  print(head(prioritized_tbl))
}, error = function(e) {
  message("Step 12 (extended prioritization) failed - likely a nichenetr version/signature difference: ",
          conditionMessage(e))
})
```

## Infer signaling paths from top ligands to target genes

```{r step13_signaling_path, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 13: Infer Signaling Paths from Top Ligands to Target Genes
#-----------------------------------------------
# Load the ligand-TF matrix — a prebuilt matrix (ligands x TFs) encoding
ligand_tf_matrix <- readRDS(file.path(model.cache.dir, "ligand_tf_matrix_human.rds"))

# Choose a top ligand to trace the signaling path
top_ligand <- best_upstream_ligands_focused[1]

# Choose the top predicted target gene for that ligand (from Step 9)
top_target <- active_ligand_target_links_df %>%
  filter(ligand == top_ligand) %>%
  arrange(desc(weight)) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  pull(target)

# ADDED: check that a ligand and a target were found
stopifnot(length(top_ligand) == 1, !is.na(top_ligand), length(top_target) == 1)
cat("Signaling path from", top_ligand, "to", top_target, "\n")

# Infer the signaling path from top_ligand to top_target
sig_path <- get_ligand_signaling_path(
  ligand_tf_matrix  = ligand_tf_matrix,
  ligands_all       = top_ligand,
  targets_all       = top_target,
  top_n_regulators  = params$signaling.top_regulators,
  weighted_networks = weighted_networks,
  minmax_scaling    = params$signaling.minmax_scaling  # normalise edge weights for cleaner visualisation
)

# Combine both edge tables and build an igraph for visualisation
sig_path_combined <- bind_rows(sig_path$sig, sig_path$gr)

# Build igraph and visualise with ggraph
sig_graph <- graph_from_data_frame(sig_path_combined, directed = TRUE)

graph_plot <- ggraph(sig_graph, layout = "kk") +
  geom_edge_link(
    aes(edge_width = weight, edge_alpha = weight),
    arrow    = arrow(length = unit(3, "mm"), type = "closed"),
    end_cap  = circle(3, "mm"),
    color    = params$graph.edge.color
  ) +
  geom_node_point(size = 5, color = params$graph.node.color) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), repel = TRUE, size = 3) +
  scale_edge_width(range = c(0.5, 2)) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(title = paste("Signaling path:", top_ligand, "->", top_target))

ggsave(file.path(plot.dir, "signaling_path.pdf"),
       plot = graph_plot, width = 8, height = 6)
# ADDED: show the plot in the notebook
print(graph_plot)
```

## Assign top ligands to specific sender cell types

```{r step14_sender_assignment}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 14: Assign Top Ligands to Specific Sender Cell Types
#-----------------------------------------------
# Assign each top ligand to its most likely sender cell type
# based on highest average expression among all sender cell types

# Use the average expression matrix computed in Step 11
# (FIX: the article comment says "Step 12")
ligand_sender_assignment <- apply(
  ligand_expression_matrix[best_upstream_ligands, ],
  1,
  function(x) names(which.max(x))
) %>%
  enframe(name = "ligand", value = "best_sender_celltype")

# Merge with ligand activity scores
ligand_summary <- ligand_activities_focused %>%
  filter(test_ligand %in% best_upstream_ligands_focused) %>%
  rename(ligand = test_ligand) %>%
  left_join(ligand_sender_assignment, by = "ligand") %>%
  arrange(desc(aupr_corrected)) %>%
  select(ligand, best_sender_celltype, aupr_corrected, auroc, pearson, rank)

# Display the summary
print(ligand_summary)

# Save to file
write.csv(ligand_summary, file.path(result.dir, "ligand_sender_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Circos plot: which sender cell types influence which target genes

```{r step15_circos_data}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 15: Circos Plot Visualization — Which Sender Cell Types Influence Which Target Genes
#-----------------------------------------------
# Build sender → target edges:
# For each top ligand, take its top 5 target genes and
# assign the ligand's dominant sender cell type (from Step 14)
# (FIX: the article comment says "Step 15")
circos_data <- active_ligand_target_links_df %>%
  group_by(ligand) %>%
  slice_max(weight, n = params$circos.top_targets) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(ligand_sender_assignment, by = "ligand") %>%
  filter(!is.na(best_sender_celltype)) %>%
  group_by(best_sender_celltype, target) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")   # count ligands linking that sender to that target

# ADDED: nothing to draw if no edges were found
stopifnot(nrow(circos_data) > 0)

# Define colors for sender cell types
stopifnot(length(params$circos.celltypes) == length(params$circos.palette))
sender_colors <- setNames(unlist(params$circos.palette), unlist(params$circos.celltypes))

# Build color vector: senders get distinct colors, target genes stay grey
all_nodes <- unique(c(circos_data$best_sender_celltype, circos_data$target))
color_vector <- rep(params$circos.default.color, length(all_nodes))
names(color_vector) <- all_nodes
for (ct in names(sender_colors)) {
  if (ct %in% names(color_vector))
    color_vector[ct] <- sender_colors[ct]
}
```

```{r step15_circos_draw}
# ADDED: the drawing is wrapped in a function so the same plot can be written
# to a PDF (article) and a PNG (shown in the notebook); circos.clear() before
# each draw.
draw_circos <- function() {
  circos.clear()
  chordDiagram(
    x                 = circos_data,
    grid.col          = color_vector,
    transparency      = params$circos.transparency,
    annotationTrack   = "grid",
    preAllocateTracks = 1
  )
  circos.trackPlotRegion(
    track.index = 1,
    panel.fun   = function(x, y) {
      xlim        <- get.cell.meta.data("xlim")
      ylim        <- get.cell.meta.data("ylim")
      sector_name <- get.cell.meta.data("sector.index")
      circos.text(
        mean(xlim), ylim[1] + 0.1,
        sector_name, facing = "clockwise",
        niceFacing = TRUE, adj = c(0, 0.5), cex = params$circos.label.cex
      )
    },
    bg.border = NA
  )
  # receiver name from params
  title(main = paste0("NicheNet: Predicted Sender Influences on ", receiver, " Target Genes"))
}

# Draw circos plot
circos.pdf <- file.path(plot.dir, "nichenet_circos.pdf")
circos.png <- file.path(plot.dir, "nichenet_circos.png")

pdf(circos.pdf, width = 10, height = 10)
draw_circos()
invisible(dev.off())
circos.clear()

# ADDED: PNG twin for the notebook
png(circos.png, width = 10, height = 10, units = "in", res = params$plot.dpi)
draw_circos()
invisible(dev.off())
circos.clear()
```

## R sessionInfo

```{r export_sessionInfo}
session.dir <- file.path(base.dir, "sessionInfo")
if (!dir.exists(session.dir)) {
  dir.create(session.dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

write.csv(unlist(sessionInfo()), file = file.path(session.dir, "tut10_nichenet_part2_sessionInfo.csv"))
sessionInfo() |>
  capture.output(file = file.path(session.dir, "tut10_nichenet_part2_sessionInfo_summary.txt"))

sessionInfo()
```
